### MobLand — Power, Loyalty & The Criminal Underworld

MobLand (2025) follows Harry Da Souza, a highly experienced fixer who works for the powerful Harrigan crime family in London. Known for his intelligence, connections, and ability to handle dangerous situations, Harry is the man the family turns to when conflicts threaten their empire.

As tensions rise between the Harrigans and their rivals, Harry finds himself caught in a violent struggle for control. With criminal alliances breaking apart and old rivalries resurfacing, every decision carries serious consequences. His job is to protect the family, manage conflicts, and prevent situations from escalating into an all-out war.

However, the deeper Harry becomes involved in the family's power struggles, the more complicated his position becomes. Loyalty is constantly tested, trust becomes difficult to maintain, and even the people closest to him may have their own hidden agendas. As the stakes grow higher, Harry must rely on his experience and strategic thinking to keep the situation under control.

The series explores themes of loyalty, ambition, betrayal, family, and the dangerous price of power. It reveals how criminal empires can begin to collapse when greed and personal rivalries become more important than unity.

What makes MobLand compelling is watching a skilled fixer attempt to control a world where one mistake can trigger a war and even the strongest alliances can fall apart.

💬 In the criminal underworld, power belongs to the family—but survival depends on knowing whom to trust.

source_details.synopsis: MobLand is a crime drama television series created by Ronan Bennett for Paramount+. The series stars Tom Hardy as Harry Da Souza, a fixer working for the Harrigan crime family led by Conrad (Pierce Brosnan) and Maeve Harrigan (Helen Mirren). Additional main characters include Kevin Harrigan (Paddy Considine), Jan Da Souza (Joanne Froggatt), Isabella Harrigan (Lara Pulver), Eddie Harrigan (Anson Boon), and Seraphina Harrigan (Mandeep Dhillon). Guy Ritchie, Anthony Byrne, Daniel Syrkin, and Lawrence Gough serve as directors. Jez Butterworth and Bennett are credited with writing all ten episodes of the first season.
